claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi's component state migrations are a new feature (recently introduced).
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A GitHub discussion for component state migrations feedback exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering the component state migrations callback contract.
The pulumi/examples repository contains an aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration example with three programs (v1, v2, v3) and migration code.
Pulumi components let you turn a group of resources into a reusable building block that can be shared across projects and teams, with users working with inputs and outputs.
The legacy AWSX VPC component (`awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc`) manages the VPC, subnets, route tables, and gateways.

In the example's v1, the `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway; a security group sits outside the component and refers to the VPC.
Because the security group refers to the VPC's ID, replacing the VPC would mean replacing the security group too, per the AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation.
The example does not create a database.
If a database is recreated, its replacement does not automatically contain the old data.
The example's second version upgrades to the modern `awsx.ec2.Vpc` component while keeping the existing network.
The example's third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

In the example, the Pulumi resource tree in v1 uses awsx:x:ec2:Vpc, awsx:x:ec2:Subnet and awsx:x:ec2:InternetGateway component types; v2 uses awsx:ec2:Vpc with the aws:ec2 resources directly beneath it; v3 uses aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc as root with no awsx components.
Pulumi's state records both physical resources and components; each record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a cloud provider ID.
Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, while modern AWSX removes those wrappers and puts the managed resources under different parents.
In this example the Pulumi name of the subnet changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1` between legacy and modern AWSX.

Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot by themselves remove component wrappers and transfer references to replacement resources.
Pulumi resource registration accepts a `stateMigrations` option taking a migration callback, alongside an alias for the legacy component type.
A Pulumi state migration callback receives the saved state of the aliased old component followed by the state of its children.

A state migration callback returns `newState` (the complete set of records replacing the old component and its children) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to the URN that takes its place).
The example migration callback is idempotent: it does nothing if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources, and raises an error for an unexpected component type.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record and changes its URN, type, and parent while preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.

The `successors` entries let the Pulumi engine update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, so the security group's reference to the VPC remains valid and connected to the migrated VPC record retaining the same AWS VPC ID.
The example's second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and maps both the old component and its VPC child to the new VPC record, which keeps its AWS ID.
The VPC registration in the example's plain-AWS version keeps aliases for both previous component types and both migration callbacks.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next callback; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration, and after both have run both callbacks return no result on later updates.
Keeping earlier migrations with the component means its users can skip versions without editing stack state by hand.

After a state migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; in this example the preview can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Running `pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.
Before each upgrade in the example, the preview should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.

When users upgrade a component that registers a state migration in its implementation, they do not need to write the migration, attach the callback, or edit stack state; Pulumi runs the migration as part of the normal preview and update.
For an internal component change that keeps the same inputs and outputs, users can keep their existing component calls.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the state migrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent and must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.

A Pulumi component state migration (the `stateMigrations` resource option callback) is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the returned result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi option reference page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/ has a callback-api section that explains the state migration callback API.

Component state migration callback state entries use the checkpoint resource format documented in the Pulumi developer docs deployment schema (pulumi-resource-state), including fields such as `urn`, `type`, `id`, `parent`, `provider`, `inputs`, and `outputs`.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing migration results (for update plans and targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied component state migration.
